subject: Aligning data retention for partner-hosted embeddings — ops & legal review
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@vectorops.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Aligning data retention for partner-hosted embeddings — ops & legal review

Samantha — thanks again for the call yesterday. I wanted to start a short thread to align on how VectorOps will handle retention, deletion, and auditability for embeddings that Redwood customers persist to your managed index when we go to co-sell. High level asks: 

- Confirm default retention window options (30/90/365 days) and whether customers can set per-index policies.
- Describe deletion semantics (hard delete vs tombstone + GC window).
- What audit logs you retain (who requested delete, timestamp, API key, request IP).

Attaching the DPA draft and a quick retention_matrix.xlsx with how we map Redwood retention tiers to your options. Can you review and flag items that will need legal redlines? If possible, loop in your legal contact.

Next steps I propose: internal review with Redwood Legal and Partners this week, then a joint redline session next Monday. Thoughts?

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0191

From: Samantha Li <samantha@vectorops.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning data retention for partner-hosted embeddings — ops & legal review

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers from our side before legal hops in: 

- Retention windows: we support per-index TTLs at 30/90/180/365 days out of the box and custom TTLs on enterprise plans.
- Deletion semantics: our API performs a tombstone on delete + background GC after 72 hours for safe eventual consistency. We also offer a synchronous hard-delete API for compliance projects (requires elevated permissions).
- Audit logs: we retain the full audit trail for 365 days in the AC logs (who/when/endpoint/IP). Longer retention available as an add-on (encrypted at rest).

I've CC'd our Partnerships inbox; Jared (copied) is our outside counsel who helps with DPA redlines. He'll pick up legal specifics. Happy to join a redline session Monday.

—Samantha
Samantha Li

Thanks — this is promising. Laura / Vivek / Karthik: looping you in to note a few Redwood constraints and requirements for any partner-hosted index we reference from the hosted API or Dedicated customers: 

- Minimum audit retention for our baseline offering must be 365 days (we need this for customer incident reconstruction).
- For regulated customers we require a hard-delete capability that can be invoked via API + a signed acknowledgement when executed (proof of deletion).
- We also need a way to surface per-customer retention config in your admin UI or via API so CS can validate settings during onboarding.

Samantha — can VectorOps provide a short tech runbook (1–2 pages) that maps your APIs to the items above? If you have a pre-existing SOC2 evidence pack showing audit/log retention and delete workflows, that would accelerate legal review.

I'll run an internal readiness checklist after we receive the runbook so we can estimate lift for co-sell enablement.

—Rafael

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-16T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning data retention for partner-hosted embeddings — ops & legal review

Samantha / team — thanks for the initial responses. From Legal's perspective, primary items we will evaluate and likely insist on in the DPA: 

- Explicit deletion SLA and attestation: for Redwood Enterprise customers we need a vendor-provided signed attestation on demand (48 hr turnaround) confirming deletion of customer-derived embeddings and any backups.
- Audit evidence: logs for 365 days with immutable tamper-evident controls; if VectorOps offers a longer window as an add-on, please document encryption and access controls.
- Subprocessor disclosures: list of any third parties that will store or process embeddings (S3, search index providers, logging vendors).
- Right-to-audit: Redwood requires either (a) vendor self-attestation plus annual SOC2 Type II, or (b) limited-scope audit access for customers with legal justification.

Please provide the technical runbook Rafael requested and a draft subprocessor list. Jared — please advise on any standard redlines you expect on the DPA.

Regards,
